Heinrich Magnus Manske, better known by his middle and last names Magnus Manske, is a German biochemist and software developer. He researches on malaria, parasites, and microbes and participates in the development of the MediaWiki system.<ref>{{#cite:Q985}}</ref>

In 2002, he wrote one of the first versions of the software that later became [[HowItWorks:MediaWiki|MediaWiki]], as a summer project while he was studying biochemistry at the [https://uni-koeln.de/en/ University of Cologne].

In 2006, he was awarded a doctor of philosophy in biochemistry<ref>{{#cite:Q988}}</ref>. His thesis, titled [https://kups.ub.uni-koeln.de/1907/ GENtle, a free multi-purpose molecular biology tool], was essentially a presentation of the GENtle software he developed for bioinformatic research<ref>{{#cite:Q985}}</ref>.

In 2007, Magnus started working at the [https://www.sanger.ac.uk/ Wellcome Trust Sanger Institute]. He was part of the malaria team until he transferred to the parasites and microbes team in 2017<ref>{{#cite:Q985}}</ref>.

In 2025, Magnus became a software developer at the [https://www.tib.eu/de/ Leibniz center of information for technology and natural science], [https://www.uni-hannover.de/en/ University of Hannover]<ref>{{#cite:Q985}}</ref>.

Today, besides being a productive biochemistry researcher, Magnus continues to actively participate in MediaWiki development, writing, in his own words, "an unreasonable number of Wikipedia and Wikidata data tools"<ref>{{#cite:Q985}}</ref>. His most famous creations include the [https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Extension:Cite Cite extension].
